observation.visible_scene: An outdoor close view of a decorative goblet: a clear glass bowl with white internal streak/crackle patterns, supported by a golden female figurine (arms raised, holding the bowl) that forms the stem, standing on a small white base. The backdrop is blurred green foliage and a brown tree trunk.
visible_changes: The camera gradually zooms out / pulls back over the whole excerpt: at the start only the lower half of the glass bowl and the upper part of the figurine fill the frame, while by the end the entire object (bowl, full figurine, white base) is shown small and centered.

As the view widens, new elements enter the frame from the bottom and sides: the white base of the figurine, a reflective glass tabletop the object rests on, a horizontal metal railing, and a garden wall / open ground on the left.
The background shifts relative to the object (the brown trunk moves toward the right edge), consistent with the camera pulling back rather than the object moving.

The white streak pattern inside the glass bowl appears to reorient/shift across frames (more horizontal swirl early, more diagonal/vertical later), while the golden figurine itself keeps a constant frontal pose.
The goblet remains in the same horizontal position throughout; no translation of the object itself is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the goblet was being held or already resting on the table at the start of the crop (the table is only revealed later).
What produced the apparent reorientation of the internal glass pattern, and any motion before or after this segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the glass bowl rotates slowly on its stem or the changing internal pattern is purely a refraction/perspective effect of the zoom-out.
Whether the camera motion is a lens zoom or a physical pull-back; the background evidence is too blurred to be certain.
Whether the object is fully stationary on the glass table throughout (the table surface is not visible in the earliest frames).
